title: Urban growth in Kasoa, west of Accra, Ghana: Sentinel-2, 2018 to 2025

headline.label: of new urban fabric in Kasoa, west of Accra, 2018 to 2025

data: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance (Copernicus programme), bands B02, B03, B04, B08, B11 and the scene classification layer, read as windows of cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs through the Earth Search STAC API (Element 84, collection sentinel-2-l2a) on 21 November 2026: S2B_30NYM_20180127_0_L2A, S2A_30NYM_20180201_0_L2A, S2B_30NYM_20181223_0_L2A, S2A_30NYM_20250105_0_L2A, S2C_30NYM_20250204_0_L2A, S2B_30NYM_20251216_0_L2A.
method: For 2018 and 2025, took the clearest scene of each quarter (or of each listed month) when at least 60% of the window was clear: 3 and 3 scenes, at 10 m in EPSG:32630.
Masked cloud, cirrus and shadow with the scene classification layer and built a per-pixel median composite of each year, plus the highest NDVI seen in the year.
Urban fabric: local standard deviation of visible brightness over 50 m at least 0.025, highest NDVI of the year under 0.5 (so fields that turn green are excluded) and MNDWI under 0 (no water).
New = urban in 2025 only, patches under 4 pixels dropped; the opposite class (urban in 2018 only) is reported as the noise level.
limits: The rule finds urban fabric (buildings, roads, paving, yards and construction), not buildings alone, so the hectares are neither a building count nor a roof area. At 10 m, anything under about 400 m² is not reliably detected; leafy suburbs, informal roofs that look like bare ground and very bright or very dark surfaces are the usual misses and false alarms. One fixed rule is used everywhere, so accuracy differs from city to city; the noise class and the OpenStreetMap check show how much here.
